newsitem.title: UK: Stocks rise to record in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise to record in Frankfurt.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - Strength in British government bonds and continental bourses helped push shares higher, though the market was trading below its best levels of the day ahead of Wall Street's truncated post-Thanksgiving session. The FTSE 100 was up 7.8 points at 4,058.0, gaining 39.3 on the week.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index charged upwards to end floor trade at a record, with the market spurred on by stronger German government bonds and the firmness of the dollar. The DAX index closed bourse dealings at 2,845.52 points, up 28.03 points on the day and up 81.83 for the week. Later the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index closed at 2,848.84 points.

PARIS - The bourse's blue-chip index closed at its highest level this year after a rally fuelled by European bond market gains, a stronger dollar and signs that a 12-day truckers' strike was winding down. The CAC-40 index finished up 25.35 points, or 1.11 percent, at 2,315.66 a rise of 60.19 on the week.
ZURICH - Shares ended higher. The all-share SPI advanced 11.16 points to 2,492.21 a rise of 10.62 from a week ago.

TOKYO - Gains racked up on the Stock Exchange in the morning session melted away by the end of the day as profit-taking and position squaring weighed on the market in the afternoon. Buying linked to the futures market also petered out, weakening stock indices in the cash market. The Nikkei 225 average settled 15.18 points lower at 21,020.36, a fall of 195.75 from last Friday,s close.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended higher, clawing back some of Thursday's heavy losses as investors continued to see more upside in prices in the medium term. The Hang Seng index rose 83.17 points to 13,393.93 after falling 220.19 points on Thursday. Over the week, the index gained 277.14 points.

SYDNEY - The share market edged just firmer by the close with mixed performances from the leaders ensuring the market failed to escape a nine-point range established early in the day. By the close, the All Ordinaries index added 2.3 points to 2,388.6, a gain of 5.2 on the week.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended near Thusrday's closing levels in what dealers said was a non-event day. Some bargain hunting in afternoon trade helped reverse some losses in gold and industrial shares but the market struggled to find direction with Wall Street closed on Thursday night for the Thanksgiving holiday. The overall index ended off 0.2 points to 6,713.9, down 12.8 since last Friday. The industrial index lost 2.9 points to 7,997.5, up 45.5 on the week, and the gold index was down 3.0 points to 1,523.7 points, down 137.2 from a week ago.
